limitations: mixed_task cohort: every session used GPT-3, so CoAuthor is NEVER a binary fully-AI positive set.
Only the 830 sessions with released author metadata (worker_id, written_by_human) are used; 617 sessions without worker ids are excluded to keep splits author-disjoint.
development split (117 sessions) is held between train and calibration; see the v2.1 split manifest for the four-way firewall.
Reconstruction is validated against the official written_by_human (see fetch-manifest reconstruction_validation).
GPT-3 suggestions are text-davinci-002 era (2021); contribution fractions reflect that generator.

source.download_instructions: Run `python -m bench.fetch_coauthor`. The script downloads the session zip from Google Drive and the public metadata sheet, replays each session's Quill deltas to reconstruct the final text plus a per-character authorship mask (prompt/user/api), validates the reconstruction against the official written_by_human (Pearson r >= 0.95), filters degenerate sessions, and locks author-disjoint (worker_id) train/development/calibration/test splits. Clean parquet + masks live under datasets/local/coauthor/ (gitignored). Raw text is never committed.

title: CoAuthor — Human+GPT-3 collaborative writing with keystroke provenance (Lee et al. 2022)
